explain.en: A friend says heat makes particles bump into each other more, and that's why reactions go faster. Using the words “activation energy” and “fraction”, tell them what they are missing.
explain.zh: 朋友说：加热让颗粒撞得更多，所以反应变快。用上「活化能」和「比例」两个词，告诉他漏掉了什么。

home.en: Drop a fizzing tablet (vitamin C or antacid) into cold water and another into warm water, and time how long each fizzes. Then crush one and drop it into cold water: that is surface area at work.
home.zh: 一片泡腾片（维生素 C 或胃药）放进冷水，另一片放进温水，计时看各冒泡多久。再把一片压碎放进冷水：这就是表面积的作用。

title.zh: 平衡不是停了，是两边一样快

insight.en: At equilibrium the forward and backward reactions run at the same rate, so amounts stay constant while particles keep changing.
insight.zh: 平衡时正、逆反应一样快，所以各物质的量不变，但颗粒一直在变来变去。

misconception.en: At equilibrium the reaction has stopped.
misconception.zh: 达到平衡时反应就停止了。

explain.en: A friend says: “At equilibrium nothing is happening any more.” Use the tagged particles and the two event counts to explain why that is wrong.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「到了平衡，就什么也不发生了。」用标记的颗粒和两条变化数曲线说明他错在哪里。

home.en: Fill one glass with water and leave a second empty. Each round, move water from glass 1 to glass 2 with a wide straw (finger over the top) while a helper moves water back with a thin straw. After a dozen rounds the levels stop changing, yet water still moves both ways every round.
home.zh: 一个杯子装满水，另一个空着。每一轮你用粗吸管（手指堵住上口）把 1 号杯的水移到 2 号杯，同伴同时用细吸管往回移。十几轮后水位不再变化，可每一轮水都还在两边来回流。

title.en: Why the table has rows and columns
title.zh: 周期表为什么有行有列

insight.en: Elements in a column behave alike because they have the same number of outer electrons.
insight.zh: 同一列的元素性质相似，因为最外层电子数一样。

misconception.en: The periodic table is ordered by atomic mass.
misconception.zh: 元素周期表是按原子质量排的。

explain.en: Sodium and potassium react fiercely with water, but magnesium barely does, even though magnesium sits between them by mass. Explain why using outer electrons and shells, not mass.
explain.zh: 钠和钾遇水反应都很剧烈，镁却几乎不反应，虽然按质量镁就夹在它们中间。用最外层电子和电子层（而不是质量）解释为什么。

home.en: Write the first 20 element symbols on 20 cards with their mass. Lay them in a line by mass, then by atomic number. Which two cards change place? Now deal them into rows of 2, 8, 8, 2.
home.zh: 在 20 张卡片上写前 20 种元素的符号和相对原子质量。先按质量排成一行，再按原子序数排。哪两张换了位置？再按 2、8、8、2 分成几行。

title.en: New stuff, or the same stuff changed?

insight.en: A change is chemical only when a new substance forms; melting, boiling and dissolving keep the same molecules, burning makes new ones.
insight.zh: 只有生成了新物质才是化学变化；熔化、沸腾、溶解后分子还是原来的分子，燃烧则造出了新分子。

misconception.en: Bubbles, a colour change or a substance vanishing always mean a chemical reaction, so boiling and dissolving are chemical changes.
misconception.zh: 冒泡、变色或东西不见了就一定是化学变化，所以沸腾、溶解也是化学变化。

explain.en: A friend says: “The sugar disappeared in my tea, so dissolving is a chemical change.” What evidence would you show them?
explain.zh: 朋友说：“糖在茶里不见了，所以溶解是化学变化。”你会拿什么证据说服他？

home.en: Stir a teaspoon of sugar into a little water and leave it on a saucer for a few days. What is left when the water has gone? Could you get baking soda back after pouring vinegar on it?
home.zh: 把一小勺糖搅进少量水里，倒在小碟子上放几天。水干了以后剩下什么？醋倒在小苏打上以后，还能把小苏打变回来吗？

title.en: What does a nail need to rust?

insight.en: Iron rusts only when water and oxygen are both present; take away either one and the nail stays almost bright.
insight.zh: 铁要同时碰到水和氧气才会生锈；去掉其中任何一个，铁钉几乎一直亮。

misconception.en: Water alone makes iron rust, so a nail fully under water always rusts.
misconception.zh: 光有水铁就会生锈，所以泡在水里的铁钉一定会锈。

explain.en: Tube B used boiled water and an oil layer. What would go wrong with only the boiling, or only the oil?
explain.zh: B 管既把水煮沸，又盖了一层油。如果只煮沸、或者只盖油，各会出什么问题？

home.en: With an adult: put three plain steel nails (not shiny galvanised ones) in three jars. One in tap water; one in water you have just boiled and cooled, with a layer of cooking oil on top; one dry, with a silica-gel packet and a lid. Look every day for a week.
home.zh: 请大人陪着：把三根普通铁钉（不要亮闪闪的镀锌钉）放进三个瓶子。一个倒自来水；一个倒刚煮沸又放凉的水，水面盖一层食用油；一个不放水，放一包硅胶干燥剂再盖上盖。一周里每天看一次。

title.en: A mole is a number, like a dozen

insight.en: A mole is a fixed count of particles, 6.02 × 10²³; a mole of magnesium weighs twice a mole of carbon because each magnesium atom is twice as heavy.
insight.zh: 1 摩尔是固定的颗粒个数 6.02 × 10²³；1 摩尔镁的质量是 1 摩尔碳的两倍，因为每个镁原子就重一倍。

misconception.en: A mole is an amount of mass, so one mole of any substance weighs the same.
misconception.zh: 摩尔是质量单位，所以任何物质 1 摩尔都一样重。

explain.en: A friend says 1 mol of copper and 1 mol of sulfur must weigh the same because “a mole is a mole.” Explain what is the same and what is different, using the balance.
explain.zh: 朋友说：1 mol 铜和 1 mol 硫一定一样重，因为「1 摩尔就是 1 摩尔」。用天平说明，哪些相同、哪些不同。

home.en: On a kitchen scale, weigh 100 grains of rice and then 100 dried beans. Same count, different mass. Use the 100-grain mass to work out how many rice grains are in a 1 kg bag, without counting them. Chemists count atoms the same way.
home.zh: 用厨房秤称 100 粒米，再称 100 粒干豆子：个数一样，质量不一样。再用 100 粒米的质量算出一袋 1 kg 的米大约有多少粒，不用真的数。化学家数原子也是这样数的。

title.en: Why salt water carries a current and sugar water doesn't
title.zh: 为什么盐水导电、糖水不导电

insight.en: Salt is built of charged ions that come apart and move freely when it dissolves or melts; sugar dissolves as whole neutral molecules, so nothing carries the charge.
insight.zh: 盐由带电的离子组成，溶解或熔化后离子散开、能自由移动；糖溶解后还是一个个不带电的分子，所以没有东西能运电荷。

misconception.en: Salt dissolves as NaCl molecules, and a solid salt crystal conducts because it is made of ions.
misconception.zh: 盐溶解后是一个个 NaCl 分子；固体盐晶体由离子组成，所以也能导电。

explain.en: A friend says salt dissolves into tiny NaCl molecules, and that a dry salt crystal should conduct because it is made of ions. Use what the bulb did with dry salt, salt water and sugar water to explain what is wrong with both ideas.
explain.zh: 朋友说：盐溶解后变成一个个小小的 NaCl 分子；干燥的盐晶体由离子组成，所以也应该导电。用灯泡在干盐、盐水和糖水里的表现，说说这两种想法各错在哪里。

home.en: Sprinkle a few grains of salt and of sugar on a dark plate and look with a magnifier: salt grains are little cubes. Stir a spoon of each into warm water in two saucers and leave them somewhere warm for a few days. What shape comes back from the salt water?
home.zh: 在深色盘子上撒几粒盐和几粒糖，用放大镜看：盐粒是一个个小立方体。各取一勺溶进两碟温水里，放在暖和的地方几天。盐水里重新长出来的是什么形状？

title.en: Adding base: the pH jump at the end
title.zh: 加碱：最后那一下 pH 突跃

insight.en: H⁺ and OH⁻ pair into water one for one, so the pH barely moves until the counts are almost equal, then a single drop pushes it up several units.
insight.zh: H⁺ 和 OH⁻ 一对一结合成水，所以 pH 起初几乎不动，直到两者个数快相等时，一滴碱就能让 pH 跳好几个单位。

misconception.en: Each drop of base raises the pH by about the same amount, so the pH climbs steadily to 7.
misconception.zh: 每滴碱让 pH 升高差不多一样多，pH 会匀速升到 7。

explain.en: A friend adds 20 mL of base, sees the pH go only from 1.0 to about 2, and decides the base is too weak. Explain what is really happening, using the H⁺ that is left.
explain.zh: 朋友加了 20 毫升碱，pH 只从 1.0 升到 2 左右，就说这碱太弱了。用「剩下的 H⁺」跟他讲讲到底发生了什么。

home.en: Count out 1000 grains of rice as H⁺. Take away 900 (now 100 left: one pH step), then 90 (10 left: another step), then 9 (1 left: another). Each step removes less than the last; the next step would need you to remove a fraction of one grain. That last tiny amount is the single drop.
home.zh: 数出 1000 粒米当作 H⁺。先拿走 900 粒（剩 100：pH 升一级），再拿走 90 粒（剩 10：又一级），再拿走 9 粒（剩 1：又一级）。每一级要拿的越来越少；再下一级就得拿走不到一粒米。那最后一点点，就是那一滴。

tagline.en: Life is built from cells, runs on matter and energy, and changes by variation and selection.
tagline.zh: 生命由细胞搭成，靠物质和能量运转，靠变异和选择改变。

name.en: Cells are the units of life

what.en: Every living thing is one cell or many; every cell comes from another cell.
what.zh: 所有生物都由一个或许多细胞组成；细胞只能由细胞分裂而来。

what.en: Flat leaves catch light, folded gut walls absorb food, small cells exchange fast.
what.zh: 扁平的叶片好接光，折叠的肠壁好吸收，小细胞交换得快。

what.en: Atoms are reused again and again; energy enters as light and leaves as heat.
what.zh: 原子被一遍遍重复利用；能量以光进来、以热离开。

name.en: Inheritance is passed on in units
name.zh: 遗传是一份一份传下去的

what.en: Genes come in pairs and are passed on whole, not blended like paint.
what.zh: 基因成对存在、整份传下去，不像颜料那样混合。

what.en: Individuals differ; those that fit better leave more offspring; populations change over generations.
what.zh: 个体各不相同；更适应的留下更多后代；种群一代代改变。

3.zh: 生命是怎么组织起来的？

4.en: How does life continue and change?

misconceptions.en: Plants get their food and mass from the soil.
misconceptions.zh: 植物从土里吃饱、长重。

misconceptions.en: Children are a blend of their parents, like mixing paint.
misconceptions.zh: 孩子是父母的混合，就像调颜料。

misconceptions.en: Animals change because they need to: giraffes stretched their necks.
misconceptions.zh: 动物因为需要才改变：长颈鹿是伸脖子伸长的。

misconceptions.en: When you lose weight, the fat turns into energy or heat.
misconceptions.zh: 减肥时，脂肪变成了能量或热。

title.en: Zoom into a leaf, a hand, a pond
title.zh: 放大一片叶、一只手、一滴池水

insight.en: Zoom in far enough on any living thing and you find cells.
insight.zh: 任何生物放大到足够倍数，都能看到细胞。

misconception.en: Only animals are made of cells.
misconception.zh: 只有动物才由细胞组成。

explain.en: A friend says “plants aren't made of cells like we are”. Using what you zoomed into, tell them what leaf and cheek cells share, and what only the leaf cell has.
explain.zh: 朋友说「植物不像我们那样由细胞组成」。用你放大看到的东西告诉他：叶细胞和口腔细胞有哪些共同部分，哪些只有叶细胞有。

home.en: Peel the thin see-through skin from inside an onion layer, lay it flat on a window and look with a magnifier or your phone's zoom. Can you see brick-like cells? Then try a drop of puddle water.
home.zh: 从洋葱鳞片内侧撕下一片透明薄膜，平贴在窗玻璃上，用放大镜或手机放大看。能看到砖块一样的细胞吗？再试试一滴水洼里的水。

insight.en: When a cell doubles in width, its volume grows eight times but its surface only four, so big cells cannot feed themselves.
insight.zh: 细胞变宽一倍，体积变 8 倍、表面只变 4 倍，太大的细胞喂不饱自己。

misconception.en: Big animals have bigger cells.
misconception.zh: 大动物的细胞更大。

explain.en: A friend says an elephant must have huge cells. Using the cube model, explain why a cell twice as wide gets hungrier faster than it can feed, and what an elephant does instead.
explain.zh: 朋友说大象的细胞一定很大。用立方体模型给他讲讲：细胞宽一倍，为什么饿得比吃得快；大象又是怎么办的。

home.en: Put a big ice cube and the same amount of crushed ice in two glasses of warm water. Which melts first? Heat gets in through the surface, like food into a cell.
home.zh: 两杯温水，一杯放一大块冰，另一杯放同样多的碎冰。哪杯先化完？热量从表面进去，就像食物进入细胞。

title.en: Where does a tree's mass come from?

insight.en: Most of a plant's dry mass is carbon taken from carbon dioxide in the air by photosynthesis, not from the soil.
insight.zh: 植物干重的大部分是光合作用从空气里的二氧化碳拿来的碳，不是从土里来的。

misconception.en: Plants get their food and mass from the soil.
misconception.zh: 植物从土里吃饱、长重。

explain.en: A friend says 'plants eat soil'. Using the willow numbers, explain where a tree's mass really comes from, and what the soil is still needed for.
explain.zh: 朋友说「植物是吃土长大的」。用柳树实验的数字给他讲讲：树的重量到底从哪里来，土又是干什么用的。

home.en: Grow cress or bean sprouts on wet paper towel, with no soil at all, for a week. They still grow. Where did their new mass come from?
home.zh: 在湿纸巾上种水芹或豆芽，一点土都不用，养一周。它们照样长大——新长的重量从哪里来？

title.en: Where does fat go when you lose weight?

insight.en: Most of the mass of burned fat leaves the body as carbon dioxide you breathe out; the rest leaves as water.
insight.zh: 烧掉的脂肪大部分变成二氧化碳从嘴里呼出去，其余变成水排出。

misconception.en: When you lose weight, the fat turns into energy or heat, or leaves through the toilet.
misconception.zh: 减肥时，脂肪变成了能量或热，或者从厕所排掉了。

explain.en: A friend says lost fat “turns into energy”. Using the 10 kg example, explain where its atoms actually go, and why the energy cannot account for the missing mass.
explain.zh: 朋友说减掉的脂肪「变成了能量」。用 10 千克的例子给他讲讲：脂肪的原子到底去了哪里，为什么能量解释不了少掉的质量。

home.en: Breathe onto a cold mirror: the mist is water leaving you. Then count your breaths for one quiet minute and use 0.04 g of CO₂ per breath to estimate how long it takes to breathe out 1 kg of CO₂.
home.zh: 对着冰凉的镜子哈一口气：那层雾就是从你身体出去的水。再安静地数一分钟呼吸次数，按每次呼出 0.04 克 CO₂，估算呼出 1 千克 CO₂ 要多久。

title.zh: 孟德尔的豌豆：为什么是 3 : 1？

insight.en: Each parent passes on one of its two copies of a gene at random, so a hidden trait comes back in about a quarter of the grandchildren.
insight.zh: 父母各随机传一份基因，所以隐藏的性状会在大约四分之一的孙代里重新出现。

misconception.en: Children are a blend of their parents, like mixing paint.
misconception.zh: 孩子是父母的混合，就像调颜料。

explain.en: A friend says children are a mix of their parents, like paint. Use the white flowers that came back in the grandchildren to explain why that can't be the whole story.
explain.zh: 朋友说孩子是父母的混合，就像调颜料。用孙代里重新出现的白花，给他讲讲为什么这种说法不对。

home.en: Give each parent a coin: heads = P, tails = p. Toss both coins together 40 times and tally how often you get pp. Do you get about 10?
home.zh: 每个亲本用一枚硬币：正面 = P，反面 = p。两枚硬币一起抛 40 次，记下 pp 出现几次。是不是 10 次左右？

insight.en: No individual changes; the mix of a population shifts because some variants leave more offspring than others.
insight.zh: 没有哪个个体自己变了；是有的变异留下的后代多，种群的组成才一代代偏移。

misconception.en: Animals change because they need to: giraffes stretched their necks.
misconception.zh: 动物因为需要才改变：长颈鹿是伸脖子伸长的。

explain.en: A friend says giraffes got long necks by stretching to reach leaves, and passed the stretch on. Use the tagged moth to explain what is wrong with that, and what happens instead.
explain.zh: 朋友说长颈鹿的脖子是为了够树叶伸长的，再把伸长传给了孩子。用被标记的蛾子给他讲讲这种说法错在哪里，真正发生的是什么。

home.en: Punch 20 dots from white paper and 20 from newspaper and scatter them on a sheet of newspaper. A "bird" picks up as many as possible in 10 s; each dot left gets one copy of its own kind added. Repeat three rounds: which kind takes over?
home.zh: 用白纸和报纸各剪 20 个小圆片，撒在一张报纸上。一个人当「鸟」，10 秒内尽量多捡；剩下的每片再加一片同样的。做三轮：哪种圆片越来越多？

title.en: From DNA letters to a protein
title.zh: 从 DNA 字母到蛋白质

insight.en: Almost every cell in your body holds the same DNA; cells differ by which genes they read, three letters (a codon) per amino acid.
insight.zh: 身体里几乎每个细胞的 DNA 都一样；细胞不同，是因为读的基因不同，三个字母（一个密码子）对应一个氨基酸。

misconception.en: Different cells in the body have different DNA.
misconception.zh: 身体里不同的细胞有不同的 DNA。

explain.en: A friend says a nerve cell has "nerve DNA" and a skin cell has "skin DNA". Use the idea of genes being switched on and off to explain why that is wrong, and name one exception.
explain.zh: 朋友说神经细胞里是「神经 DNA」，皮肤细胞里是「皮肤 DNA」。用「基因的开和关」给他讲讲为什么不对，再说出一个例外。

home.en: Write a sentence of three-letter words: THE CAT ATE THE RAT. Change one letter: how much of the meaning survives? Now delete one letter near the start and regroup into threes. Which mistake does more damage, and why?
home.zh: 用三个字母的英文单词写一句话：THE CAT ATE THE RAT。改一个字母，意思还剩多少？再在开头附近删掉一个字母，重新三个一组地读。哪种错误破坏更大？为什么？

title.en: Why does a potato shrink in salt water?
title.zh: 土豆条为什么在盐水里变软变轻？

insight.en: Particles never stop moving; water crosses a cell membrane both ways, and the net flow is towards the side where water is scarcer, the saltier side.
insight.zh: 颗粒从不停止运动；水在细胞膜两边来回穿过，净流向是水更少、也就是更咸的那一边。

misconception.en: Once the concentrations are equal on both sides, the particles stop moving.
misconception.zh: 两边浓度一样以后，颗粒就不动了。

explain.en: A friend says that once both sides are equal, the water stops moving. Use the crossing counters to explain what really happens, and why a potato strip in salt water loses mass.
explain.zh: 朋友说：两边一样以后水就不动了。用穿膜计数器给他讲讲到底发生了什么，再讲讲土豆条泡在盐水里为什么变轻。

home.en: Cut two equal potato sticks. Put one in plain water and one in water with 2 big spoons of salt. After an hour, bend them: which is floppy? Weigh them if you have a kitchen scale.
home.zh: 切两根一样的土豆条，一根泡清水，一根泡加了两大勺盐的水。一小时后弯一弯，哪根软塌塌？有厨房秤就称一称。

insight.en: Blood goes through the heart twice per lap: the right side pumps it to the lungs, the left side pumps it to the body; it is always red, bright when full of oxygen and dark when not.
insight.zh: 血液绕一圈要经过心脏两次：右边把它泵到肺，左边把它泵到全身；血一直是红的，含氧多时鲜红，含氧少时暗红。

misconception.en: Blood without oxygen is blue; that is why veins look blue.
misconception.zh: 缺氧的血是蓝色的，所以静脉看起来是蓝的。

explain.en: A friend says blood in your veins is blue until it touches air. Explain why that is wrong, and why the pulmonary artery carries dark red blood even though it is an artery.
explain.zh: 朋友说静脉里的血是蓝的，碰到空气才变红。说说这为什么不对，再说说肺动脉明明是动脉，为什么流的是暗红色的血。

home.en: Find the pulse on your wrist; count the beats for 15 s and multiply by 4. Do 30 jumping jacks and count again. Taking about 70 mL per beat, how many litres a minute did your heart pump each time?
home.zh: 在手腕上摸到脉搏，数 15 秒的跳动次数再乘 4。做 30 个开合跳后再数一次。按每跳约 70 mL 算，两次你的心脏每分钟各泵了多少升血？

title.zh: 呼吸运动不等于细胞呼吸

insight.en: Breathing only moves air in and out of the lungs; respiration, releasing energy from glucose (almost always with oxygen), happens inside every living cell, day and night, in plants too.
insight.zh: 呼吸运动只是把空气吸进、呼出肺；分解葡萄糖、释放能量的细胞呼吸（几乎都要用氧），在每个活细胞里日夜进行，植物也一样。

misconception.en: Respiration means breathing, and it happens only in the lungs.
misconception.zh: 呼吸作用就是喘气，只在肺里发生。

explain.en: A friend says “respiration is breathing, so it happens in the lungs, and plants don't do it”. Using the oxygen trip and the leaf in the dark, explain where respiration happens and what breathing is for.
explain.zh: 朋友说「呼吸作用就是喘气，所以发生在肺里，植物也不呼吸」。用氧分子的行程和黑暗里的叶片，给他讲讲细胞呼吸在哪里发生，呼吸运动又是干什么的。

home.en: Count your breaths and your pulse for one minute sitting still, then again right after 30 jumping jacks. Both rise. Which cells asked for the extra oxygen?
home.zh: 安静坐着数一分钟呼吸次数和脉搏，再做 30 个开合跳后马上数一次。两个数都变大了。是哪些细胞要了更多的氧？

title.en: Hares and lynx: why do the numbers cycle?
title.zh: 野兔和猞猁：数量为什么一起一落？

insight.en: Predators and prey can rise and fall in repeating cycles with the predator peak arriving after the prey peak, because predators multiply only after food is plentiful and starve only after it is gone.
insight.zh: 捕食者和猎物的数量可以周期性起落，捕食者的高峰总比猎物晚到：食物多了它们才多起来，食物没了它们才饿下去。

misconception.en: In nature, populations stay at a fixed balance, or predators simply eat their prey until it is gone.
misconception.zh: 自然界的种群数量保持固定的平衡，或者捕食者会一直吃到猎物灭绝。

explain.en: A friend says lynx should just eat hares until there are none left. Using the loop, explain why the lynx crash before the hares run out, and why their peak comes after the hares' peak.
explain.zh: 朋友说猞猁应该一直吃到野兔一只不剩。用那个圈给他讲讲：为什么野兔还没吃光猞猁就先大跌，为什么猞猁的顶峰在野兔之后。

home.en: Play “hares and lynx” with dried beans (hares) and coins (lynx) on a table: each round every hare has a baby, each lynx eats one hare if it can, a lynx that ate 3 hares has a kitten and one that ate none dies. Count both after each round and plot them. Do you see the lynx peak late?
home.zh: 在桌上用豆子当野兔、硬币当猞猁玩「兔和猞猁」：每轮每只兔生一只，每只猞猁能吃就吃一只兔，吃满 3 只的猞猁生一只幼崽，一只没吃到的饿死。每轮数一数两种各有多少，画成图。猞猁是不是晚到顶？

insight.en: Body temperature and blood sugar stay near a set point because any change switches on a response that pushes it back: negative feedback.
insight.zh: 体温和血糖能稳在一个设定值附近，是因为任何偏离都会触发一个把它拉回来的反应：这就是负反馈。

misconception.en: Negative feedback means something bad, and a healthy body's levels never move.
misconception.zh: 负反馈就是坏事；健康的身体里各项指标一点都不变。

explain.en: A friend says "negative feedback" must be something bad, and that a healthy person's temperature never changes. Using what happened when you stepped into the cold, explain what negative feedback really is and why the number still moves.
explain.zh: 朋友说「负反馈」肯定是坏事，而且健康人的体温一点都不会变。用你走进寒冷时看到的结果，给他讲讲负反馈到底是什么，为什么数值还是会动。

home.en: Measure your temperature under the tongue when you wake up, after lunch and in the evening, three days in a row, and plot it. Does it stay at exactly 37.0? (Use the same thermometer; wait 15 min after eating or drinking.)
home.zh: 连续三天，在起床后、午饭后和晚上各量一次舌下体温，画成折线。它是不是一直正好 37.0？（用同一支体温计；吃喝后等 15 分钟再量。）

tagline.en: Read the map, then ask why this place is the way it is.
tagline.zh: 先读懂地图，再问这个地方为什么是这样。

name.en: A map is the world made small

what.en: Scale, direction and a key — and every map has to leave things out.
what.zh: 比例尺、方向、图例；地图总要舍掉一些东西。

name.en: Places differ, and there are reasons
name.zh: 地方和地方不一样，有原因

what.en: Latitude, land and sea, and relief shape climate; climate shapes how people live.
what.zh: 纬度、海陆、地形决定气候；气候决定人怎么生活。

what.en: Spinning gives day, night and time zones; orbiting with a tilted axis gives seasons.
what.zh: 自转带来昼夜和时区；公转加上地轴倾斜带来四季。

name.en: People change places, and places change people
name.zh: 人改变环境，环境也改变人

what.en: Cities, farming, taming rivers — and what each of them changes back.
what.zh: 城市、农业、河流治理，以及它们反过来带来的变化。

2.en: Why is it hot here and cold there?

3.en: Why do people here live the way they do?
3.zh: 这个地方的人为什么这样生活？

misconceptions.en: Summer is when Earth is closer to the Sun.
misconceptions.zh: 夏天是因为地球离太阳近。

misconceptions.en: North always means 'up', on a map and on the ground.
misconceptions.zh: 北就是「上面」，地图上是，地上也是。

misconceptions.en: A mountain top should be warmer, because it is closer to the Sun.
misconceptions.zh: 山顶离太阳更近，应该更暖和。

misconceptions.en: When it is daytime for me, it is daytime everywhere.
misconceptions.zh: 我这里是白天，全世界都是白天。

misconceptions.en: A country with more young people simply has more people.
misconceptions.zh: 年轻人多的国家只是人多而已。

title.en: Draw a map of my home

insight.en: A map shrinks every distance by the same number; the scale tells you that number.
insight.zh: 地图把所有距离都缩小同样的倍数，比例尺就是这个倍数。

misconception.en: Things on a map are drawn as big as they look important.
misconception.zh: 地图上的东西越重要画得越大。

explain.en: A friend draws their bedroom bigger than the whole kitchen because it is their favourite room. Explain why a real map can't do that. Use the word "scale".
explain.zh: 朋友把自己的卧室画得比整个厨房还大，因为那是他最喜欢的房间。用「比例尺」这个词，说说真正的地图为什么不能这样画。

home.en: Measure your room in steps or with a tape. Draw it on squared paper where 1 cm on the paper = 50 cm in the room. Measure your bed on the paper, multiply by 50, and check with the real bed.
home.zh: 用步子或卷尺量你的房间。在方格纸上画出来：纸上 1 厘米 = 房间里 50 厘米。在纸上量你的床，乘 50，再去量真床对一对。

insight.en: Seasons come from Earth's tilted axis (about 23.44°): it changes how high the noon Sun climbs and how long the day lasts. Distance barely matters — Earth is closest to the Sun in early January.
insight.zh: 四季来自地轴倾斜（约 23.44°）：它改变正午太阳有多高、白天有多长。距离几乎不起作用——地球在一月初离太阳最近。

misconception.en: Summer is when Earth is closer to the Sun.
misconception.zh: 夏天是因为地球离太阳近。

explain.en: A friend says summer is when Earth is closer to the Sun. Use one fact about January and one about Australia to change their mind.
explain.zh: 朋友说夏天是因为地球离太阳近。用一条关于一月的事实、一条关于澳大利亚的事实，说服他。

home.en: Shine a torch straight down on paper, then at a slant, and trace the bright patch each time. The slanted patch is bigger, so each bit of paper gets less light. Bonus: measure your noon shadow once a month.
home.zh: 用手电筒垂直照一张纸，再斜着照，每次描出亮斑。斜照的亮斑更大，每一小块纸分到的光更少。加分：每月量一次正午时自己的影子。

title.en: Why is it night in New York when it's day in Beijing?
title.zh: 北京白天时，纽约为什么是夜里？

insight.en: Earth turns 15° every hour, so every 15° of longitude is one hour of sun time; time zones round this to whole hours and follow borders.
insight.zh: 地球每小时转 15°，所以经度每差 15°，太阳时就差 1 小时；时区把它取整成整点，并沿着国界划分。

misconception.en: When it is daytime for me, it is daytime everywhere.
misconception.zh: 我这里是白天，全世界都是白天。

explain.en: A friend in Beijing wants to video-call a cousin in New York after school at 17:00. Explain why the cousin might still be in bed, using the 15°-per-hour rule.
explain.zh: 北京的小朋友想放学后 17:00 和纽约的表哥视频。用「每小时 15°」解释：为什么表哥那时可能还在睡觉？

home.en: In a dark room, shine a torch at a ball (or an orange with a sticker on it). Turn the ball slowly from west to east and count how far the sticker turns before it comes back into the light.
home.zh: 在黑屋里用手电筒照一个球（或贴了小贴纸的橙子）。从西往东慢慢转球，数一数贴纸要转多远才回到亮处。

title.en: Why is it cold on a mountain top?

insight.en: Air is warmed mostly by the ground below, and it cools by about 6.5 °C for every kilometre you climb.
insight.zh: 空气主要被地面加热，每升高 1 千米大约降温 6.5 °C。

misconception.en: A mountain top should be warmer, because it is closer to the Sun.
misconception.zh: 山顶离太阳更近，应该更暖和。

explain.en: A friend says mountain tops should be warm because they are closer to the Sun. Use the 6.5 °C-per-kilometre rule and the "closer to the Sun" numbers to explain why Kilimanjaro has ice although it is almost on the equator.
explain.zh: 朋友说山顶离太阳更近，应该更暖和。用「每千米降 6.5 °C」和「离太阳近了多少」的数字，解释为什么几乎在赤道上的乞力马扎罗山顶也有冰。

home.en: In a weather app, find two places near each other at different heights (a town and a nearby mountain or hill station). Compare their temperatures at the same time, and work out how many °C colder it is per 1,000 m.
home.zh: 在天气 App 里找两个离得近、但高度不同的地方（比如一座城市和附近的山顶或山区小镇）。比较同一时刻的气温，算一算每升高 1000 米冷了多少度。

title.en: Read a place from its climate graph
title.zh: 从气候图读出一个地方

insight.en: Twelve bars of rain and a line of temperature tell you the climate type, and the climate tells you what grows there.
insight.zh: 十二根降水柱加一条气温线，就能判断气候类型，气候又告诉你那里长什么。

misconception.en: Places at the same latitude have the same climate.
misconception.zh: 同一纬度的地方气候都一样。

explain.en: A friend says Beijing and Lisbon must have the same weather because both are near 40°N. Use the two climate graphs to explain why you would pack an umbrella for Lisbon in January but for Beijing in July.
explain.zh: 朋友说北京和里斯本都在北纬 40° 附近，天气一定一样。用两张气候图解释：为什么去里斯本要在一月带伞，去北京要在七月带伞？

home.en: Find your town's monthly rain and temperature on a weather service's climate page and draw its climate graph on squared paper: 12 bars and one line. Which of the five types is it closest to? What do farmers grow nearby?
home.zh: 在气象部门网站的「气候」页面查家乡每个月的降水和气温，在方格纸上画出气候图：12 根柱、一条线。它最像五种气候里的哪一种？附近的农民种什么？

title.en: What a population pyramid tells you
title.zh: 人口金字塔告诉你什么

insight.en: The shape of the pyramid shows today's births and deaths and predicts the population of the next 30 years.
insight.zh: 金字塔的形状反映今天的出生和死亡，也预示未来 30 年的人口。

misconception.en: A country with more young people simply has more people.
misconception.zh: 年轻人多的国家只是人多而已。

explain.en: A friend says: “Country A only has more young people — that's all.” Use the words ‘parents’ and ‘in 25 years’ to explain what the wide base means for the future.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「A 国只是年轻人多而已。」用「父母」和「25 年后」这两个词，讲讲底部宽对将来意味着什么。

home.en: List the ages of everyone in your extended family (grandparents to cousins). Sort them into 10-year groups and draw your family's own pyramid. Who will be the parents in 20 years?
home.zh: 列出大家庭里每个人的年龄（从祖父母到表兄弟姐妹），按 10 岁一组分好，画出你家自己的金字塔。20 年后谁会当父母？

title.zh: 为什么沙漠多在 30° 附近

insight.en: Air rises at the hot equator, drops its rain, and sinks dry around 30° north and south — where most big deserts are.
insight.zh: 空气在炎热的赤道上升、把雨下完，在南北纬 30° 附近干燥地下沉——大沙漠多在那里。

misconception.en: Deserts are where it is hottest.
misconception.zh: 沙漠就是最热的地方。

explain.en: A friend says the Sahara is a desert because it is so hot. Explain, using rising and sinking air, why the even hotter equator is rainy and the Sahara is dry.
explain.zh: 朋友说撒哈拉是沙漠，因为它太热了。用空气的上升和下沉解释：为什么更热的赤道多雨，撒哈拉却干？

home.en: Hold a glass of iced water near the steam from a hot drink (or breathe on a cold mirror): cooling air drops its water as drops. Then warm the misted mirror with a hair-dryer — warming air takes the water back.
home.zh: 把装冰水的杯子靠近热饮冒出的水汽（或对着冷镜子哈气）：空气变冷，水汽变成水珠。再用吹风机吹热这块雾面——空气变暖，水又被带走。

insight.en: Earthquakes and volcanoes line up along the edges of plates, so a map of them draws the plates for you.
insight.zh: 地震和火山沿板块边缘排成带，把它们画在地图上，板块就显出来了。

misconception.en: Earthquakes can happen anywhere equally.
misconception.zh: 地震在哪里都一样容易发生。

explain.en: A friend says an earthquake is just as likely anywhere. Use the dot map to explain why Japan and Chile get big quakes but central Australia almost never does.
explain.zh: 朋友说地震在哪里都一样容易发生。用这张地震点图向他解释：为什么日本和智利常有大地震，澳大利亚中部却几乎没有？

home.en: Put two crackers side by side on a plate. Push them together, pull them apart, slide them past each other. Where do the crumbs and cracks appear — in the middle or at the edges?
home.zh: 把两块饼干并排放在盘子里。把它们推到一起、拉开、再错开滑动。碎屑和裂缝出现在哪里——中间还是边上？

insight.en: North is a direction on the ground, not "up": turn the map until its north arrow points north, then a letter and a number pin down any square.
insight.zh: 北是地上的一个方向，不是「上面」：把地图转到指北针朝北，再用一个字母加一个数字，就能说清任何一格。

misconception.en: North always means 'up', on a map and on the ground.
misconception.zh: 北就是「上面」，地图上是，地上也是。

explain.en: A friend holds the park map with the N arrow pointing at their feet and says: "North is up, so the pond is straight ahead." Tell them how to find which way north really is, and how "B4" helps them find the pond.
explain.zh: 朋友拿着公园地图，N 箭头朝着自己的脚，却说：「北就是上面，所以池塘就在正前方。」告诉他怎样找到真正的北，以及「B4」怎样帮他找到池塘。

home.en: Draw your room on squared paper. Write A, B, C… across the bottom and 1, 2, 3… up the side, and add an N arrow (a phone compass can tell you north). Hide a toy and give a grown-up the square, like "C2". Then turn the paper round: is your N arrow still right?
home.zh: 在方格纸上画你的房间。底下横着写 A、B、C……，旁边往上写 1、2、3……，再画一个 N 箭头（手机指南针能告诉你哪边是北）。藏一个玩具，告诉大人它在哪一格，比如「C2」。然后把纸转个方向：你的 N 箭头还对吗？

title.en: Read a hill from its contour lines
title.zh: 从等高线看出山的样子

insight.en: Each contour line joins points of the same height, so lines packed close together mean a steep slope and lines far apart mean gentle ground.
insight.zh: 每条等高线连起同样高的点，所以线挤在一起是陡坡，线稀疏是缓坡。

misconception.en: Contour lines that are close together show low, flat ground.
misconception.zh: 等高线挤在一起的地方又低又平。

explain.en: A friend says crowded contour lines must mean low, flat ground. Explain what the gap between two contour lines measures, and what on a map tells you whether ground is low or high.
explain.zh: 朋友说等高线挤在一起的地方一定又低又平。讲清楚：两条等高线之间的距离量的是什么？要知道地面高还是低，该看地图上的什么？

home.en: Make a clay hill with one steep side, stand it in a clear box and add water 1 cm at a time, tracing the waterline on the hill each time. Look straight down: where are the lines closest?
home.zh: 用黏土捏一座一边陡、一边缓的小山，放进透明盒子，每次加 1 厘米水，沿水边在山上画一圈。从正上方往下看：哪里的线最密？

title.en: Why one side of the mountain is dry
title.zh: 为什么山的一边是干的

insight.en: Wind pushes moist air up the windward side, where it cools and rains; the air that comes down the other side is dry and warming, so the leeward side lies in a rain shadow.
insight.zh: 风把湿空气推上迎风坡，空气变冷就下雨；翻过山顶下来的空气又干又在变暖，所以背风坡落在「雨影」里。

misconception.en: Rain falls evenly on both sides of a mountain range.
misconception.zh: 山两边下的雨一样多。

explain.en: A friend says rain falls evenly on both sides of a mountain range. Use the words “rises”, “cools”, “cloud” and “sinks” to explain why the town behind the mountains is dry, and why it is also warmer.
explain.zh: 朋友说山脉两边下的雨一样多。用「上升」「变冷」「成云」「下沉」这几个词，解释为什么山后面的小镇很干，而且还更暖和。

home.en: On a rainfall map of your country (a weather service's climate map or an atlas), find a mountain range. Which side is greener on the map? Check which way the wind usually blows there: is the wet side facing the wind?
home.zh: 在一张全国降水分布图上（气象部门的气候图或地图册），找一道山脉。图上哪一边更绿、雨更多？查一查那里平常刮什么方向的风：湿的那一边是不是正对着风？

insight.en: In a bend the water runs fastest on the outside, which wears the bank away, and slowest on the inside, which drops sand — so bends grow and wander.
insight.zh: 在河湾里，外侧水流最快，冲刷河岸；内侧水流最慢，泥沙堆积——所以河湾越来越弯，还会慢慢移动。

misconception.en: A river wears away both banks of a bend equally.
misconception.zh: 河湾两边的岸被冲刷得一样多。

explain.en: A friend wants to build a house right at the edge of a river bend, on the outside, for the view. Use what you saw to explain what may happen, and where you would build instead.
explain.zh: 朋友想把房子盖在河湾外侧的岸边，因为风景好。用你看到的现象跟他解释可能会发生什么，你会把房子盖在哪里。

home.en: In a sandpit or a tray of damp sand, scrape a curved channel and pour water slowly in at one end. Where on the curve is sand washed away, and where does it settle?
home.zh: 在沙坑里或一盘湿沙上划出一条弯弯的小河道，从一头慢慢倒水。弯道的哪一边沙子被冲走，哪一边沙子沉下来？

title.en: Is Greenland as big as Africa?
title.zh: 格陵兰岛有非洲那么大吗？

insight.en: A round Earth cannot be flattened without stretching; the Mercator map keeps directions true but blows up areas near the poles, so Greenland looks like Africa although Africa is about 14 times larger.
insight.zh: 球面摊平一定会被拉伸；墨卡托地图保住了方向，却把靠近两极的面积放大，所以格陵兰看起来和非洲差不多，其实非洲约是它的 14 倍。

misconception.en: Countries on a world map are shown at their true relative sizes.
misconception.zh: 世界地图上各国的大小就是它们真实的大小比例。

explain.en: A friend says Greenland is about as big as Africa, because that is how it looks on the classroom map. Explain why the map makes it look so big, and how many Greenlands really fit into Africa.
explain.zh: 朋友说格陵兰岛和非洲差不多大，因为教室墙上的地图就是这样画的。向他解释：为什么地图把格陵兰画得这么大？非洲里其实能放下几个格陵兰？

home.en: Draw a few same-size circles on an orange: one near the “equator”, one near the top. Peel it and press the peel flat. Which circle tears or stretches more?
home.zh: 在橘子上画几个一样大的小圆：一个在“赤道”附近，一个在顶部附近。剥下橘子皮压平。哪个圆被撕开或拉得更厉害？

tagline.en: Time has length, and we know the past from evidence.
tagline.zh: 时间有长度，过去要靠证据来认识。

what.en: How long a hundred or a thousand years is; what was happening in different places at the same time.
what.zh: 一百年、一千年有多长；同一时间世界各地在干什么。

name.en: How do we know about the past?

what.en: Objects, documents and sites; the closer a source is to the event, the more it is worth questioning carefully.
what.zh: 文物、文献、遗址；离事件越近的材料越值得追问。

what.en: Long-term causes, triggers and chance; technology, environment and people.
what.zh: 长期原因、直接原因、偶然；技术、环境、人。

name.en: How did people see it then?

what.en: Don't judge people of the past by today's knowledge; different people at the same event tell it differently.
what.zh: 不用今天的眼光要求古人；同一事件不同当事人说法不同。

2.en: How far away is the past?

3.en: Why should we believe this happened?
3.zh: 我们凭什么相信这件事？

4.en: Why did it happen this way, and how else could it have gone?
4.zh: 为什么会这样，还可能怎样？

misconceptions.en: Everything ‘ancient’ happened at about the same time — the past is one big ‘long ago’.
misconceptions.zh: 「古代」的事都差不多同时发生，过去就是一整团「很久以前」。

misconceptions.en: If an old book or inscription says it, it must be true.
misconceptions.zh: 古书或碑文上写的，就一定是真的。

misconceptions.en: Every event has one single cause.
misconceptions.zh: 每件事都只有一个原因。

misconceptions.en: People in the past were less clever than us.
misconceptions.zh: 古人没有我们聪明。

title.en: How long ago is long ago?

insight.en: Time has length: written history is a thin slice, and civilisations overlapped in surprising ways — Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
insight.zh: 时间有长度：有文字的历史只是薄薄一层，各地文明的时间交错得出人意料——克娄巴特拉离登月比离修建大金字塔还近。

misconception.en: ‘Ancient’ events all happened around the same time; the past is one undifferentiated ‘long ago’.
misconception.zh: 「古代」的事都发生在差不多的时候，过去就是一整团「很久以前」。

explain.en: Explain to a friend how one ‘ancient’ person can be closer in time to us than to another ‘ancient’ person. Use the numbers from the timeline.
explain.zh: 给朋友讲讲：为什么一位「古人」离我们，可能比离另一位「古人」还近？用时间线上的数字说明。

home.en: Make a timeline from a long strip of paper: 1 cm for every 100 years. Mark your own birth, a grandparent's birth and three events from this page. How long must the strip be to reach the Great Pyramid?
home.zh: 用一长条纸做时间线：每 100 年 1 厘米。标出你的出生、祖辈的出生和本页的三件事。纸条要多长才能到达大金字塔？

insight.en: Civilisations did not take turns: around 500 BCE Confucius in China, the Buddha in India and the citizens of Athens were alive in the same few generations.
insight.zh: 各地文明不是轮流登场的：公元前 500 年前后，中国的孔子、印度的佛陀和雅典的公民生活在相隔不过几代人的时间里。

misconception.en: History happened one civilisation after another, like chapters in a book.
misconception.zh: 历史是一个文明接一个文明发生的，像书的一章接一章。

explain.en: A friend says “first came China, then India, then Greece, then Rome”. Use two slices from this page to show them why that is not quite right.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「先有中国，然后是印度，然后是希腊，然后是罗马。」用本页的两个年份切片，跟他讲清楚为什么这样说不太对。

home.en: Ask an older relative what was happening in three different countries in the year they were born. Draw three lanes on paper and mark that year with one line across all of them.
home.zh: 问一位长辈：他出生那年，三个不同国家各在发生什么？在纸上画三条横道，用一根竖线把那一年穿过三条道。

insight.en: The earliest clay tablets from Mesopotamia mostly record goods, rations and accounts — writing began as a tool for keeping track, not for telling stories.
insight.zh: 美索不达米亚最早的泥板大多记的是货物、口粮和账目——文字一开始是记账的工具，不是讲故事的。

misconception.en: Writing was invented to record stories and poems.
misconception.zh: 文字是为了写故事和诗歌才发明的。

explain.en: A friend says “writing was invented so people could write down stories and poems.” Use what you found on this page, with one number, to explain what the earliest writing was for and why it was needed.
explain.zh: 朋友说「文字是为了写故事和诗歌才发明的」。用本页的发现和一个数字给他讲清楚：最早的文字是干什么用的，为什么需要它。

home.en: Ask someone to read you 10 shopping items with amounts (3 apples, 2 loaves…) without you writing. Write down what you remember. Then do it again with tally marks and a little picture for each item. Which list is right?
home.zh: 请家人念 10 样要买的东西和数量（3 个苹果、2 个面包……），你不许写，念完把记得的写下来。再来一遍，这次边听边画记号和小图。哪一张单子对？

title.en: How old is it? Tree rings and radiocarbon
title.zh: 它有多老？树轮和放射性碳

insight.en: Carbon-14 in once-living things halves about every 5,730 years, so what is left works like a clock; tree rings, counted year by year, check and calibrate that clock.
insight.zh: 曾经活着的东西里的碳-14 大约每 5730 年减少一半，剩下多少就像一只钟；一年一圈的树轮用来校准这只钟。

misconception.en: Scientists just guess how old ancient things are.
misconception.zh: 科学家只是猜古物有多老。

explain.en: A friend says “archaeologists just guess the age of bones and charcoal.” Explain, with one number from this page, how the carbon-14 clock works and why tree rings are needed to check it.
explain.zh: 朋友说「考古学家只是猜骨头和木炭有多老」。用本页的一个数字给他讲清楚：碳-14 的钟怎么走，为什么还要用树轮来校准。

home.en: Look at a tree stump or a log end. Count the rings from bark to centre, and find the narrow ones. Then take 64 coins, shake them in a box and remove the tails; repeat. How many shakes until about 1/4, 1/16 are left?
home.zh: 找一个树桩或木头的断面，从树皮往中心数年轮，找出窄的那几圈。再拿 64 枚硬币放进盒子里摇，拿掉反面朝上的，重复。摇几次后大约剩 1/4、1/16？

insight.en: Every source was made by someone, at some time, for some purpose; asking who, when and why tells you what the source can and cannot show.
insight.zh: 每份史料都是某人、在某时、为某个目的留下的；问清谁、何时、为什么，就知道它能说明什么、不能说明什么。

misconception.en: If it is written in an old source, it must be true.
misconception.zh: 古代材料上写的，就一定是真的。

explain.en: A classmate says: “The ballad is very old, so its number must be right.” Use two other sources to answer them: who made each, when, and why?
explain.zh: 同学说：「这首歌谣很古老，所以它的数字一定对。」用另外两份材料回答他：每份是谁、何时、为什么写的？

home.en: Find two accounts of the same family event (a photo caption, a message, someone's memory). For each ask who made it, when and why. Where do they disagree, and which would you trust for what?
home.zh: 找两份讲同一件家庭往事的材料（照片说明、一条消息、一个人的回忆）。每份都问：谁、何时、为什么留下的？哪里说法不同？各自在哪方面更可信？

title.zh: 丝绸之路上走的是什么？

insight.en: The Silk Roads were a web of routes; goods, ideas, religions and inventions passed hand to hand through chains of traders, and few people travelled the whole way.
insight.zh: 丝绸之路是一张路网；货物、思想、宗教和发明经过一段段商人接力传递，很少有人走完全程。

misconception.en: The Silk Road was one road that merchants travelled from end to end.
misconception.zh: 丝绸之路是一条路，商人从头走到尾。

explain.en: A friend says “a merchant took silk along the Silk Road from China to Rome”. Use the trader counter and the price from this page to explain what really happened, and why the price went up so much.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「一个商人沿着丝绸之路把丝绸从中国运到了罗马。」用本页的经手人数和价格，跟他讲讲实际是怎样的，价格为什么涨了那么多。

home.en: Play “pass it on” with your family: whisper a short message along a line of people, or pass a cup of rice and let each person keep one spoonful as their “fee”. How much arrives at the end of 3 people? Of 6?
home.zh: 和家人玩「传下去」：沿一排人悄悄传一句话；或者传一杯米，每人留一勺当「辛苦费」。经过 3 个人还剩多少？6 个人呢？

title.en: Why did printing spread so fast?
title.zh: 印刷术为什么传得那么快？

insight.en: Big changes rarely have one cause: long-term conditions, a trigger and people's choices work together, and taking one away changes the outcome.
insight.zh: 大变化很少只有一个原因：长期条件、直接诱因和人的选择一起起作用，拿掉一个，结果就会不同。

misconception.en: Every event has one single cause.
misconception.zh: 每件事都只有一个原因。

explain.en: A friend says: “Gutenberg invented printing, end of story.” Use two other causes from this page — and what you learned about Bi Sheng and the Jikji — to give a fuller answer.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「古腾堡发明了印刷术，就这么简单。」用本页另外两个原因，再加上毕昇和《直指》的事，给他一个更完整的回答。

home.en: Pick a change in your family or school (a new shop nearby, a new club, a new habit). Draw a causes web with at least one long-term condition, one trigger and one choice. Ask someone who was there: which one, taken away, would have changed the most?
home.zh: 挑一件家里或学校发生的变化（附近开了新店、新办了一个社团、养成一个新习惯），画一张原因网：至少一个长期条件、一个诱因、一个人的选择。问问当时在场的人：拿掉哪一个，结果会变得最多？

title.en: Dig down, go back in time

insight.en: Layers of soil pile up over time, so deeper usually means older — but a pit dug from above can carry newer things down, and a layer can be no older than the newest object in it.
insight.zh: 土层是一层层堆上去的，所以越深通常越老——但从上面挖下来的坑会把新东西带到深处，而一层土的年代不会早于其中最新的那件东西。

misconception.en: Anything found deeper in the ground is always older, and everything in one layer is the same age.
misconception.zh: 埋得越深的东西一定越老，同一层里的东西年代都一样。

explain.en: A friend says: “This coin was found deeper than that pot, so it must be older.” Use the pit or the burrow from this page to explain why that is not always true, and say how you would date the layer instead.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「这枚硬币比那块陶片埋得深，所以一定更老。」用本页的坑或动物洞给他解释为什么不一定，再说说你会怎样给那一层定年代。

home.en: In a clear cup, make layers of rice, lentils, flour and coffee grounds. On each layer drop a paper “coin” with a year, older years lower down. Then dig a “pit” with a spoon from the top and drop in a coin with this year. Is the deepest coin still the oldest? Date each layer by its newest coin.
home.zh: 在透明杯子里铺几层：米、扁豆、面粉、咖啡渣。每铺一层放一张写着年份的纸「硬币」，越往下年份越早。然后用勺子从上往下挖一个「坑」，放进一枚写着今年的硬币。最深的硬币还是最老的吗？用每层最新的硬币给它定年代。

insight.en: A year number is only a count from a chosen starting point: BCE/CE counts from one fixed year with no year 0, the 干支 cycle repeats every 60 years, and regnal years restart with each ruler — to convert you need an anchor that links them.
insight.zh: 年份只是从某个起点数下来的数：公元从一个固定年份数起、没有公元 0 年；干支每 60 年循环一次；年号纪年每换一个皇帝或年号就重新数——换算要靠一个把它们连起来的「锚点」。

misconception.en: People everywhere always counted years the same way we do, and there was a year 0 between 1 BCE and 1 CE.
misconception.zh: 古今各地的人都像我们这样数年份，而且公元前 1 年和公元 1 年之间有个「公元 0 年」。

explain.en: Someone says, “In ancient China they wrote 629 on things too.” Explain what they would really have written, and how a historian turns it into 629.
explain.zh: 有人说：「古代中国人也在东西上写 629。」讲讲当时的人其实会怎么写，历史学家又是怎么把它换算成 629 的。

home.en: Ask three family members the year they were born and work out its 干支 (stem = (Y − 4) mod 10, branch = (Y − 4) mod 12). Who shares a branch, and how many years apart are they? Then make a 10-ring and a 12-ring from paper and turn them together.
home.zh: 问三位家人出生的年份，算出它们的干支（天干 = (Y − 4) 除以 10 的余数，地支 = (Y − 4) 除以 12 的余数）。谁的地支相同？相差几年？再用纸做一个 10 格圆环和一个 12 格圆环，一起转一转。

title.en: Where did your dinner come from?

insight.en: Many ‘traditional’ foods depend on crops that crossed the oceans between the Americas and the rest of the world only after 1492: chilli, potato, tomato, maize and sweet potato came from the Americas, while wheat, rice, sugar cane, cattle and horses went the other way.
insight.zh: 许多「传统」饭菜靠的是 1492 年以后才在美洲和世界其他地方之间跨洋交换的作物：辣椒、土豆、番茄、玉米、红薯来自美洲，小麦、水稻、甘蔗、牛和马则去了美洲。

misconception.en: Foods that are central to a cuisine today — chilli in Sichuan or Korean cooking, tomatoes in Italian cooking — have always grown there.
misconception.zh: 今天某地菜系的招牌食材——川菜和韩国菜里的辣椒、意大利菜里的番茄——从来就长在那里。

explain.en: A friend says chilli is a traditional Chinese spice, so it must have grown in China forever. Explain where chilli came from, when it is first recorded in China, and why a ‘traditional’ food can still be fairly new.
explain.zh: 朋友说辣椒是中国传统香料，一定自古就长在中国。跟他讲讲：辣椒从哪里来，中国最早什么时候有记载，为什么一种「传统」食物也可能挺新的。

home.en: List the ingredients of tonight's dinner. Guess for each: from the Americas, or from Africa, Europe and Asia? Look them up. How many would be missing in 1400?
home.zh: 列出今天晚饭的食材，每一样先猜：来自美洲，还是亚非欧？再查一查。放到 1400 年，会少几样？

title.en: Two people saw it — and told it differently
title.zh: 两个人都看见了，说法却不一样

insight.en: Each eyewitness saw from one place, at one moment, with their own concerns, so honest witnesses can disagree; the parts that independent accounts share are the firmest evidence.
insight.zh: 每个目击者都只在一个位置、一个时刻、带着自己的关心在看，所以诚实的人也会说法不同；几份互不相干的说法都对得上的部分，才是最站得住的证据。

misconception.en: If two eyewitnesses disagree, one of them must be lying.
misconception.zh: 两个目击者说法不一样，就一定有一个在说谎。

explain.en: A friend says: “The apple seller and the neighbour disagree, so one of them is a liar.” Use the plan to show how both could be honest, and say which record settles who helped.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「苹果摊主和邻居说法不一样，所以有一个是骗子。」用这张平面图说明两人怎么可能都诚实，再说说哪份记录能定下到底有没有人帮忙。

home.en: Ask two people at home, separately, to describe the same moment (a meal, a trip). Sketch where each sat or stood and what each could see. Which details do both tell? Which only one?
home.zh: 请家里两个人分别讲同一个时刻（一顿饭、一次出门）。画个草图，标出每人坐或站在哪、能看见什么。哪些细节两人都讲了？哪些只有一人讲？

title.en: What changed, and what stayed the same?

insight.en: Different parts of life change at different speeds: how fast people could travel or how they lit their homes changed within a few generations, while staple foods, languages and family customs often lasted for centuries.
insight.zh: 生活的不同方面变化速度不同：出行多快、晚上用什么照明，几代人之内就变了；而主食、语言和家庭习俗常常延续几百年。

misconception.en: The past was one unchanging ‘before’, and modern times changed everything at once.
misconception.zh: 过去是一成不变的「从前」，到了近代一下子什么都变了。

explain.en: A friend says: “In the old days nothing changed, then modern times changed everything.” Use two rows from the board — one that changed fast and one that hardly changed — to answer them.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「从前什么都不变，到了近代一下子全变了。」用变化板上的两行——一行变得快、一行几乎没变——来回答他。

home.en: Ask an older relative to compare their childhood with today for: travel, lighting, the main food, how news arrives, a family festival. Which changed a lot, and which stayed the same?
home.zh: 请一位长辈比较他小时候和现在：出行、照明、主食、怎么得到消息、一个家里过的节日。哪些变了很多，哪些没变？

tagline.en: Break it into exact steps, let loops do the repeating, and hunt the bug calmly.
tagline.zh: 把大事拆成准确的小步骤，重复的交给循环，出错了就一步步找。

name.en: Break a big job into small steps

what.en: Brushing your teeth is a list of instructions too; get the order wrong and the result is wrong.
what.zh: 刷牙也是一串指令；顺序错了结果就错。

name.en: Hand repeated work to a loop

what.en: Four times 'forward, turn right' is a square.
what.zh: 走 4 次「前进 + 右转」就是正方形。

name.zh: 一切信息都可以变成数

what.en: A colour is three numbers, text is a code, a picture is a grid of squares.
what.zh: 颜色是三个数，文字是编码，图片是格子。

what.en: Go one step at a time and see which step does something other than you expected.
what.zh: 一步一步走，看哪一步和想的不一样。

1.en: How does the robot get there?

2.en: How can we write fewer commands?

3.en: How do we make a program smarter?

misconceptions.en: The computer knows what you mean.
misconceptions.zh: 电脑知道你想让它做什么。

misconceptions.en: The order of the commands doesn't matter.
misconceptions.zh: 指令的顺序无所谓。

misconceptions.en: A program with a bug means you are bad at coding.
misconceptions.zh: 程序出错说明我不会编程。

misconceptions.en: A computer stores a picture as a picture, not as numbers.
misconceptions.zh: 电脑里存的图片就是图，不是数。

misconceptions.en: A faster computer always beats a better algorithm.
misconceptions.zh: 电脑够快，算法好不好无所谓。

insight.en: A robot only does exactly what it is told, one instruction at a time.
insight.zh: 机器人只做你说的那一句，一次一句。

misconception.en: The robot will work out what you meant.
misconception.zh: 机器人会自己明白你的意思。

title.en: Tell the robot exactly what to do

insight.en: A program is a list of exact steps run in order; when the same steps repeat, a loop says them once.
insight.zh: 程序是一串按顺序执行的准确步骤；同样的步骤重复时，用循环只写一次。

misconception.en: The computer knows what you mean, and the order doesn't matter.
misconception.zh: 电脑知道你的意思，顺序无所谓。

explain.en: Your friend wrote 'turn right, forward, forward' but meant 'forward, forward, turn right'. Explain why the robot ends up somewhere else, and how stepping through one command at a time would show the mistake.
explain.zh: 朋友写了「右转、前进、前进」，其实想写「前进、前进、右转」。说说为什么机器人会走到别处，以及一步一步执行怎样帮你找到这个错。

home.en: Put a toy at one end of a room. A grown-up plays the robot and only understands 'step forward', 'turn left', 'turn right'. Write the commands on paper first, then read them out one by one. Did the robot reach the toy?
home.zh: 在房间一头放个玩具。请大人当机器人，只听得懂「向前一步」「左转」「右转」。先把指令写在纸上，再一条条念出来。机器人走到玩具那里了吗？

insight.en: To find a bug, run one step at a time and compare what happens with what you expected.
insight.zh: 找错的办法：一步一步执行，把每一步的结果和你想的对一对。

misconception.en: If the program is wrong you have to start again from scratch.
misconception.zh: 程序错了只能全部重写。

explain.en: A friend's robot program stops one square from the star, and they want to delete it all. Explain how they can find the wrong command instead.
explain.zh: 朋友的机器人程序停在离星星一格的地方，他想全部删掉重写。跟他说说怎样找到错的那一条。

home.en: Write directions from your bed to the kitchen. Ask someone to follow them, one line at a time, while you watch. Where do they first go wrong? Change only that line.
home.zh: 写一份从床边走到厨房的路线。请家人一行一行照着走，你在旁边看。他第一次走错是在哪一行？只改那一行。

insight.en: A regular shape with n sides is 'forward, turn 360°/n' repeated n times.
insight.zh: 正 n 边形就是把「前进、转 360°/n」重复 n 次。

misconception.en: To draw a hexagon the turtle turns by the hexagon's inside angle, 120°.
misconception.zh: 画六边形时，海龟每次转的是六边形的内角 120°。

explain.en: A friend says a 10-sided shape needs 20 commands. Show them a loop that draws it, and explain why the turn has to be 36°.
explain.zh: 朋友说画正十边形要写 20 条指令。写一个循环给他看，并说说为什么每次要转 36°。

home.en: Be the turtle: walk 4 steps, turn right a quarter turn, and do it 4 times. Then walk a triangle. How far do you turn at each corner? At the end, check that you face the way you started.
home.zh: 自己当海龟：走 4 步，向右转四分之一圈，做 4 遍。再走一个三角形：每个拐角要转多少？走完看看你是不是又朝着开始的方向。

title.en: A picture is a grid of numbers

insight.en: A screen picture is a grid of pixels, and each pixel's colour is three numbers: red, green, blue.
insight.zh: 屏幕上的图是像素格子，每格的颜色是红、绿、蓝三个数。

misconception.en: A computer stores a picture as a picture, not as numbers.
misconception.zh: 电脑里存的图片就是图，不是数。

explain.en: A friend says “the computer just saves the photo”. Explain what it really saves, and why a white pixel is (255, 255, 255).
explain.zh: 朋友说「电脑就是把照片存起来」。说说它真正存的是什么，以及为什么白色像素是 (255, 255, 255)。

home.en: Look at a screen through a magnifying glass, or put a drop of water on a phone screen showing white: on many screens you will see tiny red, green and blue lights.
home.zh: 用放大镜看屏幕，或者在显示白色的手机屏幕上滴一小滴水：很多屏幕上能看到很小的红、绿、蓝小灯。

insight.en: In binary each place is worth twice the place to its right, so any whole number is a sum of 1, 2, 4, 8, ….
insight.zh: 二进制每一位是右边一位的两倍，所以任何整数都能写成 1、2、4、8……的和。

misconception.en: Binary is a secret code only computers can read.
misconception.zh: 二进制是只有电脑才看得懂的密码。

explain.en: A friend says binary is a secret code only computers understand. Use the dot cards to show them how to read 10110, and why each card has twice the dots of the card to its right.
explain.zh: 朋友说二进制是只有电脑才看得懂的密码。用点点卡给他演示怎样读 10110，并说说为什么每张卡的点数是右边那张的两倍。

home.en: Draw five cards on paper with 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 dots. Ask someone for a number up to 31 and make it by turning cards over; then count from 0 to 31 together, flipping cards as you go.
home.zh: 在纸上画五张卡，分别画 1、2、4、8、16 个点。请家人说一个不超过 31 的数，你翻卡把它拼出来；再一起从 0 数到 31，边数边翻卡。

insight.en: Different step-by-step methods give the same sorted list but need very different numbers of comparisons.
insight.zh: 不同的排序方法排出同样的结果，但比较的次数可以差很多。

misconception.en: Any method that gets the right answer is equally good.
misconception.zh: 只要结果对，方法都一样好。

explain.en: A friend says “bubble sort works, so it’s as good as any other.” Use the numbers for 1,000 items to explain why a programmer would still pick merge sort, and say when insertion sort is the smart choice.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「冒泡排序能排对，所以跟别的方法一样好。」用 1000 个数的比较次数跟他解释，程序员为什么还是会选归并排序；再说说什么时候插入排序最划算。

home.en: Shuffle 8 playing cards face down. Sort them twice: once by comparing neighbours (bubble sort), once by sorting each half and then merging the two piles. Count the comparisons each time, with someone keeping a tally.
home.zh: 把 8 张扑克牌洗乱、背面朝上。排两次：一次只比较相邻的两张（冒泡排序），一次先把两半各自排好、再把两叠合并。请家人记下每次比较了多少回。

title.en: Halve it: how search gets fast
title.zh: 对半找：搜索为什么能这么快

insight.en: Halving a sorted list each time finds one item among a million in about 20 looks.
insight.zh: 在排好序的表里每次砍掉一半，一百万个里找一个只要约 20 次。

misconception.en: A faster computer always beats a better algorithm.
misconception.zh: 电脑够快，算法好不好无所谓。

explain.en: A friend says “just buy a faster computer, the method doesn’t matter.” Use the numbers for a list of a million to explain why halving still wins, and say when your friend is right.
explain.zh: 朋友说：「买台更快的电脑就行，方法无所谓。」用一百万个数的例子跟他解释为什么对半找还是赢；再说说什么时候他说得对。

home.en: Ask someone to think of a number from 1 to 100 and answer only “higher” or “lower”. Play once guessing freely and once always guessing the middle; count the guesses. Then find a word in a paper dictionary by opening it in the middle and halving.
home.zh: 请家人想一个 1 到 100 的数，只回答「大了」或「小了」。玩两次：一次随便猜，一次每次都猜中间，数一数各猜了几次。再用纸质字典查一个字：从中间翻开，每次扔掉一半。

title.en: Send a picture with a few numbers

insight.en: A black-and-white picture can be sent as counts of same-colour squares in a row, so a picture with long runs needs far fewer numbers and still comes back exactly the same.
insight.zh: 黑白图可以按「连续几格同色」来数着送，同色连得越长要送的数就越少，收到后还能一格不差地画回来。

misconception.en: Making a picture file smaller always loses some of the picture.
misconception.zh: 把图片文件变小，一定会丢掉一部分画面。

explain.en: Read the numbers for one heart row to a friend who can't see it. Why can they colour exactly the same row? Why does a checkerboard need more numbers?
explain.zh: 把心的某一行的数念给看不见图的朋友听。为什么他能涂出一模一样的一行？为什么棋盘格要的数更多？

home.en: On squared paper, colour a simple 10 × 10 picture. Read only the row numbers to someone at home and let them colour their own grid. Hold the two papers side by side: are they the same?
home.zh: 在方格纸上涂一张简单的 10 × 10 图。只把每行的数念给家里人听，让他在自己的格子上涂。把两张纸放在一起：一样吗？

title.en: A robot that checks for walls

insight.en: With 'if there is a wall ahead, turn; otherwise go forward' inside a loop, one short program can get through many different mazes it has never seen.
insight.zh: 把「如果前面有墙就转弯，否则前进」放进循环，一段短短的程序就能走过许多没见过的迷宫。

misconception.en: A program always makes exactly the same moves every time it runs.
misconception.zh: 程序每次运行，走的步子都一模一样。

explain.en: A friend says “a program always does exactly the same thing”. Use the wall-checking robot to explain when that is true (a plain list) and when it is not (an if inside a loop).
explain.zh: 朋友说「程序每次都做一模一样的事」。用会看墙的机器人跟他讲讲：什么时候是这样（直接列步骤），什么时候不是（循环里放「如果」）。

home.en: Draw a maze on squared paper. Move your pencil from the start, keeping a wall always on its right. Does it reach the end? Then draw a maze with a wall island where it never does.
home.zh: 在方格纸上画一个迷宫。铅笔从起点出发，始终让墙在它右边。能走到终点吗？再画一个带「墙岛」的迷宫，让它永远走不到。

title.en: The card-flip trick: catching an error

insight.en: Add one extra card to every row and column so each has an even number of black sides; then a single flipped card shows up as the one odd row crossing the one odd column.
insight.zh: 给每行每列各补一张牌，让黑面都是偶数个；之后有一张被翻，它就在唯一那条奇数行和唯一那条奇数列的交叉处。

misconception.en: To notice a mistake in a message you have to remember the whole message.
misconception.zh: 要发现信息里的错，就得把整条信息都记住。

explain.en: A friend says you can only spot a changed card if you remember the whole layout. Explain how the extra row and column let you find it, and why the trick fails when two cards are flipped.
explain.zh: 朋友说，要发现哪张牌变了，就得记住整个牌阵。给他讲讲补上的一行一列怎样帮你找到那张牌，再说说为什么翻两张就不灵了。

home.en: Use 25 coins or paper squares coloured on one side. Lay out 5 × 5 at random, then add a 6th card to each row and a 6th row so every row and column has an even number of coloured sides. Turn your back while someone flips one, then find it.
home.zh: 用 25 枚硬币，或一面涂了颜色的纸片，随便摆成 5 × 5；再给每行补第 6 张、补上第 6 行，让每行每列涂色面朝上的都是偶数个。转过身请家人翻一张，你再把它找出来。

title.zh: 变量是贴了名字的盒子

insight.en: A variable is a named box that holds one value at a time; putting a new value in throws the old one away, so swapping two boxes needs a third.
insight.zh: 变量是贴了名字的盒子，一次只装一个值；放进新值，旧值就没了，所以交换两个盒子的值要借第三个盒子。

misconception.en: Writing 'a = b' and then 'b = a' swaps the two values.
misconception.zh: 先写「a = b」再写「b = a」，两个值就交换了。

explain.en: Your friend wrote a = b and then b = a to swap two numbers, and both came out the same. Explain what happened to the first number, and how a third box fixes it.
explain.zh: 朋友想交换两个数，写了 a = b 再写 b = a，结果两个数一样了。跟他讲讲第一个数去哪了，第三个盒子为什么能解决问题。

home.en: Two cups: one with water, one with juice. Swap what is in them. What did you need? Write down each move as a line like “empty cup = water cup”.
home.zh: 两个杯子，一杯水，一杯果汁。把两杯里的东西对调。你需要什么？把每一步写成一行，比如「空杯 = 水杯」。

title.en: One artificial neuron learns to sort
title.zh: 一个人工神经元学分类

insight.en: A neuron multiplies each input by a weight, adds them up and says 'yes' if the total passes a threshold, so it splits the plane with a straight line; learning is nudging the weights after every mistake.
insight.zh: 神经元把每个输入乘上权重再相加，超过阈值就答「是」，所以它用一条直线把平面分成两边；学习就是每错一次把权重挪一点。

misconception.en: A program that learns to sort things correctly must understand them the way a person does.
misconception.zh: 能学会正确分类的程序，一定像人一样懂得它分的是什么。

explain.en: Explain to someone how this neuron gets all 16 fruits right without knowing what a fruit is. Then say why it can never get the XOR fruit all right, using the straight line.
explain.zh: 跟别人讲讲：这个神经元不知道水果是什么，为什么还能把 16 个水果全部分对？再用「直线」说明它为什么永远分不对异或水果。

home.en: Score 10 snacks from 0 to 10 for sweetness and for crunch, and plot them on squared paper: a circle if a family member likes it, a square if not. Can one ruler line split circles from squares? Try to find four snacks that no line can split.
home.zh: 给 10 种零食的甜度和脆度各打 0 到 10 分，画在方格纸上：家人喜欢的画圆、不喜欢的画方块。能用尺子画一条直线把圆和方块分开吗？试着找出四种零食，让任何直线都分不开。

why.en: Your child finds out that a robot does exactly what it is told, one instruction at a time, and nothing more.
why.zh: 孩子会发现：机器人只照你说的做，一次一句，多一点都不会。

en: a favourite soft toy
a clear path across the room
zh: 一个孩子喜欢的毛绒玩具
房间里一段没有杂物的路

en: Put the toy across the room. Say: I am a robot. I only know step, turn left, turn right.
Your child gives one instruction at a time. Do exactly that, with stiff robot moves.
If an instruction is unclear, like 'go there', freeze and say: Robot does not understand.
When the robot reaches the toy, pick it up only if your child says 'pick up'.
Swap: your child is the robot and you give the instructions.
zh: 把玩具放在房间另一头，说：「我是机器人，只听得懂『走一步』『左转』『右转』。」
孩子一次说一句，你就只做那一句，动作僵硬一点，像机器人。
听到「去那边」这种说不清的话，就停住说：「机器人听不懂。」
走到玩具旁边，要孩子说「捡起来」，你才捡。
换过来：孩子当机器人，你来下指令。

guess.en: Before you start: how many steps do you think the robot needs to reach the toy?
guess.zh: 开始前先猜：机器人要走几步才能碰到玩具？

en: Why did the robot stop?
What could you say so the robot understands?
Was it harder to give the orders or to be the robot?
zh: 机器人刚才为什么不动了？
换一句什么话，机器人就听懂了？
下指令难，还是当机器人难？

easier.en: Use only 'step' and put the toy straight ahead, a few steps away.
easier.zh: 只用「走一步」，玩具放在正前方几步远的地方。

harder.en: Put a chair in the way, so the robot has to turn to go round it.
harder.zh: 在路上放一把椅子，机器人得转弯绕过去。

watch.en: Look for the moment your child switches from pointing to choosing a word. Laugh with them when the robot walks into a wall; that is the fun part.
watch.zh: 留意孩子什么时候从用手指着，变成挑一句话来说。机器人撞到墙时一起笑一笑，这正是好玩的地方。

safety.en: Clear the path of things to trip over, and keep the robot well away from stairs and sharp corners.
safety.zh: 先把路上会绊脚的东西挪开，机器人别走到楼梯和尖角附近。

why.en: Your child sees that an everyday job is a list of small steps, and that the order changes the result.
why.zh: 孩子会看到，每天做的事也是一串小步骤，顺序换了，结果就不一样。

en: 4–5 pieces of paper
a marker or crayons
zh: 4 到 5 张纸
一支记号笔或几支蜡笔

en: Pick a routine your child knows, like brushing teeth or getting dressed to go out.
Together, draw one step on each paper: get the brush, add toothpaste, brush, rinse.
Shuffle the papers, and let your child lay them out in order on the floor.
Act out the routine by following the papers exactly, one at a time.
zh: 挑一件孩子熟悉的事，比如刷牙，或者穿衣服出门。
一起画，一张纸画一步：拿牙刷、挤牙膏、刷牙、漱口。
把纸打乱，让孩子在地上按顺序摆好。
照着纸一张一张做一遍，纸上怎么画就怎么做。

guess.en: Which step do you think comes first? Put it down, then we act it out and see.
guess.zh: 你猜哪一步排第一？先摆上，再演一遍看看对不对。

en: What happens if we brush before the toothpaste goes on?
Is there a step we forgot to draw?
Could two of these steps swap places and still work?
zh: 还没挤牙膏就刷，会怎么样？
有没有哪一步忘了画？
有没有两步换个位置也没关系？

easier.en: Use just three cards, such as put on socks, put on shoes, open the door.
easier.zh: 只用三张，比如穿袜子、穿鞋、开门。

harder.en: Draw a longer routine, like washing hands, with six or seven steps.
harder.zh: 画一件步骤更多的事，比如洗手，画六七步。

watch.en: Some steps really can swap and some cannot; if your child notices that, it is a big idea. Ask them to explain the order back to you.
watch.zh: 有的步骤能换，有的不能换。孩子要是发现了这一点，就是很大的收获。请孩子把顺序讲给你听。

why.en: Your child learns that a mistake is one wrong step you can find and fix, not a reason to start over.
why.zh: 孩子会知道：出错只是某一步不对，找到它改掉就好，不用全部重来。

en: a pair of socks and shoes, or a coat
the step cards from Steps in Order, if you made them
zh: 一双袜子和鞋，或者一件外套
如果做过「排排步骤」，把那几张卡也拿来

en: Tell your child the robot will get dressed, but there is a mistake hidden in its list.
Act out a routine with one step out of place, like putting on shoes before socks.
Go slowly, one step at a time, and let your child shout 'Stop!' at the wrong step.
Ask which step to change, fix only that one, and act it out again.
zh: 跟孩子说：机器人要穿衣服了，可是它的步骤里藏了一个错。
演一遍，故意放错一步，比如先穿鞋、再穿袜子。
一步一步慢慢演，孩子看到错的那一步就喊「停！」。
问孩子该改哪一步，只改那一步，再演一遍。

guess.en: Before the robot starts: do you think the mistake is near the start, the middle or the end?
guess.zh: 机器人开始前先猜：那个错在开头、中间，还是最后？

en: Which step was the silly one?
Did we need to change the other steps too?
How did you know that step was wrong?
zh: 哪一步是错的？
别的步骤也要改吗？
你怎么看出那一步错了？

easier.en: Make the mistake very big and funny, like a sock on your hand.
easier.zh: 错得夸张一点，比如把袜子套在手上。

harder.en: Hide a missing step instead of a swapped one, like forgetting to open the door.
harder.zh: 这次不是放错，而是少一步，比如忘了开门就往外走。

watch.en: Notice whether your child watches each step before calling out. Praise the hunt: 'You checked every step.' Then let them hide a mistake for you.
watch.zh: 看孩子是不是一步步盯着看再喊停。夸找的过程：「你每一步都看了。」再让孩子藏一个错给你找。

why.en: Your child meets a first loop: a short pattern you say once and then repeat.
why.zh: 孩子第一次碰到「循环」：一小段动作说一次，然后重复做。

en: your hands and feet
paper and a marker to draw the pattern
zh: 手和脚
一张纸、一支笔，用来画动作

en: Show a short pattern: clap, clap, stomp. Do it once slowly.
Say: Again, three times. Do the pattern three times together without stopping.
Draw the pattern once as pictures, a hand, a hand, a foot, and write '3 times' beside it.
Let your child make up a new pattern and tell you how many times to repeat it.
zh: 先做一小段：拍手、拍手、跺脚。慢慢做一遍。
说「再来，做三遍」，然后一起连着做三遍。
把这一段在纸上画一次：手、手、脚，旁边写「3 遍」。
请孩子编一段新动作，再告诉你要重复几遍。

guess.en: If we do clap, clap, stomp three times, how many claps will there be? Guess, then let's count.
guess.zh: 「拍、拍、跺」做三遍，一共拍几下手？先猜，再做一遍数数看。

en: What part keeps coming back?
Is it quicker to say the whole thing, or say it once and '3 times'?
What comes next after clap, clap, stomp, clap, clap…?
zh: 哪一段一直在重复？
从头到尾全说出来快，还是说一遍再加「3 遍」快？
拍、拍、跺、拍、拍……下一个是什么？

easier.en: Use a two-part pattern, clap, stomp, and repeat it twice.
easier.zh: 只用两个动作：拍手、跺脚，重复两遍。

harder.en: Put a loop in a walk: step, step, turn, four times. Where do you end up?
harder.zh: 走路也来循环：走一步、走一步、转身，做四遍。最后站在哪儿？

watch.en: The idea to notice is 'say it once, do it many times'. If your child starts saying 'times three' on their own, that is a loop in their words.
watch.zh: 要留意的是「说一次，做很多次」。孩子自己说出「做三遍」，就是用自己的话说出了循环。

why.en: Your child plans a whole route with arrow cards before anyone moves, then checks it one step at a time.
why.zh: 孩子先用箭头卡把整条路排好，再一步一步走，看排得对不对。

en: floor tiles, or masking tape to make a 4 × 4 grid
8–10 pieces of card with a big arrow drawn on each
a soft toy as the goal
zh: 地砖格子，或者用纸胶带在地上贴一个 4 × 4 的格子
8 到 10 张卡片，每张画一个大箭头
一个毛绒玩具当终点

en: Put the toy on one square and stand on another square, facing the same way as your child.
Your child lays arrow cards in a row: each card means one step that way.
When the row is done, walk it card by card while your child points to each one.
If you miss the toy, look together for the card where things went wrong and change it.
zh: 把玩具放在一个格子上，你站在另一格，和孩子朝同一个方向。
孩子把箭头卡排成一排，每张卡表示朝那个方向走一格。
排完了，你一张一张照着走，孩子用手指着走到哪张。
没走到玩具，就一起找是哪张卡开始走偏的，把它改掉。

guess.en: Before I walk: do you think these arrows will take me to the toy?
guess.zh: 我走之前你先猜：照这些箭头走，能走到玩具那里吗？

en: Which card made me go the wrong way?
Is there a shorter path with fewer cards?
Can you find a different path that also works?
zh: 是哪张卡让我走错了？
有没有用更少卡片的近路？
还有别的路也能走到吗？

easier.en: Put the toy in a straight line from you, so only one kind of arrow is needed.
easier.zh: 玩具放在正前方一条直线上，只用一种箭头就够了。

harder.en: Put a cushion on one square as a rock the path must go around.
harder.zh: 在一格上放个靠垫当石头，路要绕开它。

watch.en: Planning the whole path before moving is the hard part; many children want to place one card and step. Both are fine, and praise every check.
watch.zh: 先把整条路排完再走，是最难的一步；很多孩子想放一张走一格。两种都可以，每次去验一验都值得夸。

safety.en: If you cut the cards, do the cutting yourself and put the scissors away. Keep the tape grid flat so nobody trips.
safety.zh: 卡片要剪的话由大人来剪，剪完把剪刀收好。胶带贴平，别让人绊倒。
